purpose: One or more code samples of the same thing in different languages or package managers, rendered on `CodeBlock` so the docs inherit its header, copy control and syntax surface. One sample renders a block titled by a label header (the sample label, else the language's readable name: Shell, JavaScript, JSON); several render the joined tab strip. A sample's `output` — what its command prints — renders as a separate muted "Output" block under it, with no copy control, so the command block holds only what the reader runs.
useWhen: The same install command for npm, pnpm and yarn.
The same request in cURL, JavaScript and Python.
avoidWhen: For unrelated snippets — use one `CodeBlock` each.
For prose that differs per platform — use `DocTabs`.
related: CodeBlock` — the surface it renders on.
DocTabs` — alternatives that are prose, not code.
bestPractices: Label each sample with what differs (the language or the tool), not with "Example". With one sample, leave `label` empty: the header names the language.
Keep the same order across a page.
Do: set `language` on every sample, so the header reads "Shell" or "JavaScript" and the code is highlighted.
Do: keep `code` to what the reader runs or pastes; the copy control copies exactly that. A leading `$ ` prompt is drawn but never copied.
Do: put what the command prints in the sample's `output` (`{ language: 'bash', code: 'curl -I https://<your-azion-domain>', output: 'HTTP/2 200' }`), or say it in prose.
Do: show a standalone printout (a deploy log) with `kind="output"`.
Don't: write output into `code` — never `curl -I https://example.com\n# HTTP/2 200`, never `$ azion version\nAzion CLI 4.23.0`. The lint `webkit/no-output-in-command` warns on it.
Don't: turn the label header off on a docs page.
